![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14064036/assets/237856bbfdfa6c5ecaead68d257270bb86aeca666fe4170be50b88b67d3ab9de.png)

Find the volume of the solid region above.

*Hint: All surfaces, except for the right one, are parallel to the corresponding coordinate planes.*
feedback.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14064036/assets/33d937ccc1ae72f5add46a9358af4427147205a072ca2848a44d61288e705235.png)

 

Notice that our solid can be written as the type III region

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,\,0\le y\le 1+\frac{x}{2}+z},
$$

where

$$
D={(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le z\le 2}
$$

is the projection of $R$ onto the $xz$-plane, shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14064036/assets/9e7c6fad45d9d85bad5ca16a2000e4d44a1739ab70797e41ae94945a4ffb02ef.png)

Hence, the type III representation of $R$ is

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le z\le 2,\,\,0\le y\le 1+\frac{x}{2}+z}
$$

Therefore, the volume of $R$ is given by the following triple integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1+x/2+z}dy\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}[y]_{y=0}^{y=1+x/2+z}\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}(1+\frac{x}{2}+z)-0\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}1+\frac{x}{2}+z\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{[(1+\frac{x}{2})z+\frac{{z}^{2}}{2}]}_{z=0}^{z=2}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}((1+\frac{x}{2})(2)+\frac{{2}^{2}}{2})-0\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}4+x\,dx \\  & ={[4x+\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{x=0}^{x=2} \\  & =(8+2)-0 \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$
